text_fidelity_a:
Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System First, I have to say, these sound amazing for their size, picking up even most low frequencies. Crank them up, and they almost vibrate themselves off the table - you can feel the bass just by putting your hand in the open air behind them. I can say confidently that these sound better than the old Boston Acoustics computer speakers that included a small subwoofer.

They are also good looking, have a standard auxiliary input in the back for versatility, and have a headphone output in the front (still trying to figure out when that could come in handy...) They also connect easily to my BB 9700, Xoom, and Win7 PC. Surprisingly, I can even control the volume from the speakers or from the controlling device!

The one speaker has a ~1.5m cable permanently attached that ends in an RCA plug that must be plugged into the other speaker. That can be extended, of course, but somehow, this makes the whole wireless thing less impressive. Somehow, I'd like to have them both pick up Bluetooth separately, but then of course, both would need separate power supplies and receptacles. The point is, for installations such as a home computer setup, what is the point of going Bluetooth for speakers? On the other hand, it is super cool to be able to just spit music from your phone at any time.

My other qualm is that they should have grill covers; I tend to pick them both up with one hand and have to be a bit careful not to stick my finger through the cone.

Overall, I'm impressed with the technology and the product itself. If you have a good use for this particular type of product and can deal without grill covers, I'm sure you'll be happy with the purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Creative T12 Wireless Bluetooth Speaker System

Doesn't use it, just that's where he puts it when he goes to sleep. Between his pillow and the wall. And every night the iPad was sliding off the bed (even though it is in a silicone case) and I was having to dig it out in the mornings for him. Not once have I had to do this.

I had contemplated a few Pinterest 'hacks' that suggested (for example) using Command Hooks attached to the wall and then sitting the iPad down into those (the big 5# ones) hooks. Problem for us is my kid has seizures that are not well controlled by meds, so all I could 'see' in my mind's eye was him seizing and in the convulsing or 'rooting' he does with most of his seizures (or unconsciously standing up then falling back down) one of those seemingly harmless plastic Command hooks gouging his eyeball out or ripping a nostril open. (If you knew all the off the wall sh** that can and does go wrong with seizures, you'd get why all the one-in-a-billions go through my head!)

Anyway, this was the best $ I've spent in a long time. It holds the iPad without any sliding or moving (the device or the pillow) and it came in his favorite color. He loved it. I love it.

text_fidelity_a:
HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac) I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.
text_fidelity_b: HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac)

text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
Fit & Fresh Protective Laptop Sleeve with Zippered Storage Pocket, Laptop Bag fits Apple/Microsoft/Acer/Samsung/Google/Lenovo with up to 15.6" Displays, Space Dyed, Gray I have a wonderful hybrid laptop/tablet but the problem is that I needed a case that was slim, but would protect my laptop even while it was being charged. I had a few dings in it from banging on edges of things, so when I saw this, I was hoping it would be perfect. Let's see what happened..

WHAT IS THIS SLEEVE LIKE?
I have backpacks, and big cases to put laptops in, but I just wanted a protective sleeve. That is precisely what this is. It is a fabulous protective sleeve for protecting the laptop. It is lined in very soft velveteen. There is a zipper pocket on the front which has a metal zipper, but is lined with BRIGHT LIME GREEN LINING. I am sorry. I had to capitalize that because I am so excited about it. It is slick so anything put inside will slide in and out easily. It matches the small colored patch on either end of the sleeve.

The outside of the sleeve is like dark denim in color. It is tougher than denim, however. The inside is a light gray. All edges are bound in tough nylon so there are no edges to fray. Workmanship is excellent on this. It is well made.

DOES IT FIT?
My laptop is a 15inch laptop and it fits perfectly. The most exciting part is that I can leave it unzipped and it gives me the room to leave the recharging jack in the laptop so I can recharge it while protecting it. When not recharging, I can zip it shut, put the charger in the pocket and be on my way. I can also zip from both sides leaving the top open if I want and the cord can still come out for recharging. (It has a two way zipper with two zipper heads on each end).

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a protective sleeve that is fresh looking and protective, this is a winner for me. It is soft inside, bright lined outside pocket, and strong workmanship all around. I am very happy with this and highly recommend it.

MY RATING

text_fidelity_a:
Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box Photoboxes are simple things; It is usually just 5-sided box with some sort of backdrop and a strip of LED. The Heysliy Light Box Photography lightbox is just that and nothing more. Designed to be portable, the box can be folded flat and comes with a carrying bag that nicely stores everything in the kit.

Unfortunately, it's the execution of the thing that is to be desired. The box is cut from a sheet of translucent plastic then folded to form a box. The flaps are joined by a barely-tight-enough screw cap that can be easily lost because it is not actually part of the box. The plastic itself is stuff, but has an elastic memory, which means that it wants to fold back to its storage position, weakening the sides of the box unless the flaps are folded outward first. Overall, the structure is quite flimsy and can be tricky to set up.

The Heysliy lightbox comes with four backdrops made of that paper-like material that is used by some reuseable grocery bags. The colors are black, white, green, and red. The backdrop is hung by a hole cut into the material and a tab that's cut into the plastic box. Any hard tug will rip that backdrop so be careful.

So the conclusion is that the box is annoying to set up and with the LED's mounted on the inside of the box, reflections will be a big issue with this box as can be seen in my pictures (nintendo switch pictured for size reference).
text_fidelity_b: Heysliy Product Photography Light Box 16x16 Inch,Adjustable Bright Photo Box with Lights,Portable Photo Studio Light Box

I live in an area undergoing major road construction on all the highways, and I wanted the GPS to help me route around it when I run errands and go to appointments. I figured the "lifetime map updates" feature would ensure this GPS shows the latest road closures to get me through the city without trouble. WRONG.

Not only does it NOT show the ongoing road construction they started months ago near my house, but it has tried to send me off an exit on another highway that has been closed for 2+ years! And when I couldn't take that exit, it refused to reroute, and kept trying to get me to take the next exit to turn around and then sent me BACK to the long-closed exit. Almost NONE of the road closures are on the GPS map, and it will not reroute even when I hit the reroute button. It is very frustrating.

We have taken the latest map updates, and even contacted Garmin, whose response was that they were sorry they had a backlog of "a lot of updates" and they were "trying to put them in as quickly as possible" -- but sending me to an exit that's been closed over 2 years says otherwise. I HATE this GPS. I only gave it 2 stars because I like the graphics options and it lets you take screen shots of the map. If it WORKED properly, I'd say it could have been a great GPS, but it doesn't do what it promised.

WHAT IS THE CORD LIKE?
The cord itself is very well insulated with bendable material. The USB and Micro-USB connectors are very nice. They fit tightly into the outlets and don't jiggle or move around like some of the cords I have tried. My Samsung Galaxy Tab S2 does really well with it when I need to recharge. I have not used it with my phone since it is another brand, I have not checked compatibility with my transformer that the USB side plugs into yet.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
I really love this cord. It does not bend severely like the white plastic cord did, or some of the other cheaper cords have. It stays nice yet pliable too. The charging goes very well and I am quite happy with the color too. The gold is really attractive and I can always find it easily and quickly.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Time will tell but the first month of use of this cord has gone very well. The problem with bending and sharp pinches seem to be solved with this cord. Charging goes well and the connectors are solid and fit firmly without being loose.

FIVE STARS for this cord. I really like it so far.

UPDATES

text_fidelity_a:
AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+ FD4100WMGUSBX My old computer was exactly that: Old! It needed some serious work. I was running an Athlon X2 6000+ and an EVGA 9800GT. It was a great system back in the day! But, time took its toll. I was kicking around the idea of getting an Intel i3, since they seem to edge out this chip, and are competitively priced (I never overclock my equipment, so it's at stock settings.) But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!
text_fidelity_b: AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+  FD4100WMGUSBX

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change) This review is of the 64GB SDHX card. I use it for a specific purpose: backing up my document folders on my two laptops. It works perfectly with my Windows XP systems over ancient USB 2.0 ports. I can still back up a full card in less than an hour, and if I were on a more modern system with USB 3.0 it would take only a fraction of that time.

This particular card will NOT work in my Samsung Galaxy Note II (I had to try anyway). In fact, make sure your device will actually accept SDHX cards before purchaing this 64GB model or you may be disappointed. Most Microsoft Windows systems running XP service pack 2 or later, Windows CE and Server 2003 will recognize this card, as will Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6.5 or later. Phones, tablets and devices running Microsoft Windows RT will also recognize this card. Beyond that check first.

Back to how I use this card: the price for this card is around forty bucks at the time of this review. I could have gotten an exernal hard drive in the terabyte range for twice that, but this has no moving parts, fits in my wallet and with a [[ASIN:B00FSDKBYY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 Flash Memory Card Reader]] plugs into any computer (with an operating system that supports the format) via USB ports. For me it's convenient, especially since I am only backing up working documents and never come close to the 64GB capacity (which is closer to 56GB formatted.) In fact I use two of these in rotation for safety, overwriting the older one completely since it takes less than an hour. I always keep the other one on my person.

As the SDHX standard becomes more established and ubiquitous this type of card may work with more devices. At 64GB this is probably the smallest size since the SDHX format was designed to accomodate up to two terabytes. So unless you have a device that is compatible with this format, or you are using it for a single purpose on a supported operating system, you may want to get an SDHC card instead.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change)

text_fidelity_a:
Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Inspection Camera, AsperX Endoscope Borescope, 8MM 1080P HD Snake Camera with Front-View & Side-View Dual Camera 6 LED Lights, 16.4 ft Cable, IP67 Waterproof, 32 GB Card

text_fidelity_a:
Eton - American Red Cross ZoneGuard Weather Radio, White, Siren/Buzzer (90dB), 3 Color LED Alert Light Bar, LCD Display, Detachable Stand, AC Power Adapter, AA Battery Operated I like the basic design of this -- the small sleek size, nice layout of buttons, large display. The radio reception seems to be decent, although mounting it on the wall is not possible in my area, since I have to turn it various directions to get a couple of local AM stations. Weather band reception is OK, as is FM reception.

That's about where my positive feelings for this little radio end.

It is way too difficult to set up, NOT with regard to the physical aspects of hitting the correct buttons in the correct sequence, but rather in terms of deciphering and understanding the instructions. The instruction leaflet, such as it is, is written in such small type that it's nearly impossible to read. I finally went to the Eton website and downloaded the instruction manual there, then "zoom"ed it so I could read how to set the time, store radio stations, etc.

Then there's the issue of the S.A.M.E. codes. I had never heard of this technology before I got this radio. NO WHERE in the included instructions is there any mention of NOAA, or even the "S.A.M.E." designation. On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions.

This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county.

And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. DISABLE: Displays the message on the LCD when receiving a message" -- does that mean that when it's enabled, you DON'T get a message displayed on the LCD when receiving a message? What kind of Alert happens when it's enabled? the flashing light? the siren? what, precisely, am I "defeating" with this??)

I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. We've had one National Weather Service-issued high wind warning here in the Pacific NW since I received and programmed the radio, and it didn't set off the alert -- no light flashing, no "message," nothing. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works.

Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.
text_fidelity_b: Eton - American Red Cross ZoneGuard Weather Radio, White, Siren/Buzzer (90dB), 3 Color LED Alert Light Bar, LCD Display, Detachable Stand, AC Power Adapter, AA Battery Operated

text_fidelity_a:
RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I dislike reviews where the comments just gush about the product. But I have no other choice but to do just that - these are some incredibly good earphones!

I've been using RHA earphones for a couple of years and have been impressed by the sound quality given the price. I own several earphones, but the ones I reach for most often by far are my RHA MA350s even though they are one of the least pricey pair of buds I own. Great sound quality and excellent build quality.

Well, the MA350s will be spending some time on the shelf. The MA750s are a clear step up. (Gush alert:) These are simply amazing! They can handle anything I thrown at them so far, with great bass that doesn't boom or bottom out, clear midrange and sharp upper range. Just fantastic performance.

I was a bit concerned about the ear wrap design since I usually find that type of design to be irritating for long-term use, and especially irritating when wearing them while exercising. But no problems at all even with extended wearing. Very comfortable and no chafing even when running.

The MA750s come with an extensive set of replacement ear cushions in a variety of designs. I can't imagine that a person would not be able to adjust these to fit perfectly given there are 10 different potential configurations. The cord is stout but flexible, with significant reenforcements at the plug end.

Even the packaging is upscale, with a high quality box with a front panel (with a magnetic enclosure) that opens to revel the earphones and tips nicely displayed. Very Apple-esque in their presentation.

Also included is a leather (or what feels like leather) carry case. The tips come with a metal holder that fits into the case so you can keep everything neatly stored and protected. A small point, but is shows that some real thought went into every aspect of this product.

While these are priced higher than other RHA earphones, the cost is well worth it. Even at the current price point, these outperform my Bose, Shure and Sennheiser earbuds that are priced far higher, and way outperform buds in their MA750 price range.

Huge recommendation for these - try as I might, I just can't find a single criticism to voice about them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Seiki SE401GS 40-Inch 1080p 120Hz Slim LED HDTV This led tv is much better than I expected it to be for the price I paid for it. I was not in the market for a new television, but the one I had in my bedroom died. It's a small room, and the dead tv was 26 inches. I started looking for something around that size and stumbled on this one for not too much more than a smaller one. So, I figured I'd give it a try, and if I liked it, I'd put the 32 inch tv from my living room in the bedroom.

Set up was very easy. I put it together using the stand. I had enough screws. They all fit. You have to screw them all the way in straight, or the tv kind of wobbles on the stand, but once I did that, the thing is very stable.

It has one component input, one composite, one antenna, one VGA, and three hdmi, and I'm using all of them. Very very easy. the whole thing, including moving the other tv, took half an hour, with the only slight pain being that my late 2010 Mac Mini won't under scan at 1080p, so I had to go to 720p, on the hdmi connection. I don't even know what any of that means, except that this is what I had to do in order to be able to see my menu bar.

Picture is really nice for the price, even my little intel atom its box over the VGA looks good. What impressed me most is the sound. I only use the tv's speakers for the Wii U, and they are surprisingly clear. I'm still figuring out some of the settings, but up and running in half an hour and enjoying the results is pretty amazing - especially for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Seiki SE401GS 40-Inch 1080p 120Hz Slim LED HDTV

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

Patriot LX Series 64GB High Speed Micro SDXC Class 10 UHS-I Transfer Speeds For Action Cameras, Phones, Tablets, and PCs So I bought this to use with my 128GB Lenovo Yoga as a secondary drive. When I plugged it into my computer to transfer some files, it shows 116GBs - what it should be for a 128GB drive. Though I really wish computers and manufacturers would calculate memory the same, that is another matter.

I went to transfer a folder with 61 GBs of memory. It got about 3/4 done and it decided it was full. With about 50GBs, my 116 GB card is FULL. It should be only about half full. This is a problem. I am not happy about this and will not buy another one of these. I will format it and try again. Maybe there are hidden files that aren't showing up on it. But this is really annoying.

Update: I decided to format the drive and found that the bit size for exFAT is very small. As in less than my file size small. I changed it to NTSF, as it will only be used in a computer, and it is now working properly as regards to being able to actually fill it with 116 GBs. But it still took about 4 hours to copy 8 GBs of data to it. My USB 3.0 drive would have done it in less than 30 minutes.

text_fidelity_a:
Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it. Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 550VA UPS Battery Backup, 300W Eco Green, USB, RJ11, 8 Outlets (ECO550UPS), Black

NVIDIA Shield TV | 4K HDR Streaming Media Player The world's first all-in-one Plex box, the Shield comes w/ an unlockable (free) Plex Server inside --and not just another client/player like all other consoles. For those of us w/ a LOT of media, Plex is the pinnacle of enjoying your own media with the best interface possible (and it's free); whereas KODI is the best way for streaming media from the internet. The Shield recognized my old archives instantly, and also when I plugged in a USB3 SanDisk flash drive for extra space. I've had 3 WDTVs, 2 Nexus Players, and 1 MiBox, and I wasted all of that time and money until I got this. I've KODI Phoenix and Exodus for internet streaming, and Plex for my 200 movies, 25 seasons of TV shows, 75 instructional videos (on guitar, magic, and yoga), 6k songs, and all my family albums and artwork. I have the Plex client (player) for TV, phones/tablets, XBox 360, Chromebooks, and Chromebox.

The Shield has BOTH the Play Store and the NVidia Store on its dashboard. I can play all my games again because this console doesn't stutter and freeze up. I'd missed my Asphalt 8 when the others just couldn't handle the workload anymore. I can get even better games from the NVidia Store that the Play Sore doesn't have. Of course, all previous purchases come right back to the Shield --like the HomeRun HD. Plex has a deal they're making w/ HomeRun HD to possibly turn the shield into also doing DVR.

The gamepad has been totally redesigned and has gone from an Ugly Duckling to being prettier than a pail full of kittens. The hex-grip feels good in the hand for shooting zombies or driving on racetracks. The gamepad is rechargeable (yay!) and even comes w/ it's own charging cable. The once $50-extra remote is now included w/ the console. Like the gamepad, the remote also has a headphone jack for discreet listening and a touchscreen volume control and Mute.
text_fidelity_b: NVIDIA Shield TV | 4K HDR Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band I have owned this watch for a year and a half now. I use it almost daily for my walks/runs, weight workouts, and indoor bike workouts. The main reason I chose this watch in the first place was because it was one of the smaller ones available. I am 5'9 but have small wrists, and really disliked the 'utilitarian' look of larger watches. After a year and a half, I am so tired of the issues with it and ready to jump ship. If I used this watch more regularly (I only wear it for workouts - not all day), I would have switched a LONG time ago. The amount of people who have complained about the same issues for YEARS without Garmin doing anything makes me hesitant to purchase another Garmin product, especially with the Apple Watch, Samsung, and now Google buying out Fitbit and coming up with a watch.
- Spotify on this watch seriously sucks. If you check Spotify forums, you will find COUNTLESS threads of suggestions for the Spotify app on this watch that should truly be basic features at this price. Do they implement them or listen? No. Also, there is no way to contact Spotify customer service - you just get pointed towards their 'community forum' where you have people complaining of the same exact things with no fix. You can't skip forward on any track, at all. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I walk. Some are 2 hours in length while my walk is only 1 hour. This watch constantly either reverts to the very beginning of my podcast so I have to start all over (because again, you can't skip forward - so have fun listening to ads as well!) in anything, only updates 1 song out of 15 on my playlist or get the error 'sync failed', or some other random issue. Also, if you have a playlist on Spotify, you cannot choose the track you want to listen to. You have to hit the >> button to get to where you want. Really? I hope Garmin drops Spotify because they have been a truly horrible app on this watch the entire time with no effort to make updates. Take a look at the reviews of Spotify on the Garmin store if you don't believe me.
- Battery life is a couple of days. However, there are points in time where my watch will be at say 80% the night before, I get ready to leave and go my walk the next morning, pick up my watch, and it's at 8%. WTF? This happens enough to be super annoying and apparently is not an 'only me' problem. It appears to be tied to when the watch updates.
- I tried to wear this to track my sleep in the beginning and gave up after two nights due to the extreme disco effect of the 'gesture' motions. I tried turning on the 'do not disturb' function advertised on the watch which is supposed to disable this stupidly bright light that WILL wake you and whoever is next to you up. Didn't work. Do a search for 'Garmin watch lights up in middle of the night' and you will find all sorts of people complaining of the same thing, and not just on this version of the watch.
- GPS has issues connecting and can take several minutes which is pretty annoying when you try to start tracking an activity only to see a red bar when trying to connect. I 'sync' my watch to my phone constantly so that is not the issue. I have switched between the GPS options Garmin offers on the watch to no avail. Search for this issue as well and you will see lots of people with the same complaint.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory Recording my listening experience with the Sennheiser HD 598 which I bought after breaking my pair of HE-400 headphones. I own Grado Labs SR80, BModed Fostex T50, Sennheiser HD-600, Hifiman HE-500.

Hour 1:
Pro: Looks good for plastic and reasonably comfortable.
Con: heavy handed, muddy, base reminds me of a one-note subwoofer, and the signature reminds me of a cheap pair of Skullcandy headphones. You could get better sound from a pair of Beat headphones. I am feeling ripped off and don't recall the last time listening to music made me MAD!
One word: Garbage!

Hour 10:
The headphones have opened up some. Vocals feel recessed. Bass still feels one dimensional. Upgraded rating from one to two stars.

Hour 15:
I am baffled by the positive reviews of this product. Yes, headphones and their sound signatures are very much a personal preference, but these are so grossly bad that I can only assume my ears are damaged or the headphones are defective. Returning them to Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

text_fidelity_a:
EagleTec HUB3639 USB 2.0, 4 Port Hub, Ultra Slim Compact USB Hub for Laptop PC Computer (Black) Since my MacBook Air has only 2 USB ports, and I have a bunch of external devices and gizmos that need to talk to the Mac via USB, I set out looking for something that would allow me to attach multiple USB-connectable devices at the same time. One of the 2 MacBook Air USB ports is dedicated to my 1TB external hard drive, but I also have a wireless mouse, a 25-key midi keyboard that I use for composing music, and a few other things that I may not use every day, but that I want to be able to use without having to disconnect my mouse.

Saw this, read the reviews, and decided to give it a try. So far, we've been working together comfortably for just over a week with no hiccups or mishaps. I like the small size -- it's small and relatively "flat," so it stays tucked just behind my laptop on my desk without occupying too much real estate. I like that.

I have the wireless mouse "receiver" plugged into the end, my midi keyboard plugged into the first of the 3 slots on the side, and I can add anything else (iPhone for syncing, etc.) in one of the other two slots. This summer, I'll be using it with a USB-driven personal fan when the weather warms up (no air conditioning here in the Pacific NW). I did test all 4 ports, and they are all working just fine.

Very happy with it so far. If I start noticing any issues, I'll update this review.
text_fidelity_b: EagleTec HUB3639 USB 2.0, 4 Port Hub, Ultra Slim Compact USB Hub for Laptop PC Computer (Black)

I bought one and it didn't work well. I hoped it was a fluke, sent it back and ordered another one. Nope. Not a fluke. This product is just a piece of junk. I wanted a device that would allow me to record from the radio but wasn't bulky (or expensive). Well, I guess there's a reason this is the cheapest alternative on the market for that demand. I got messages saying that my media was being refreshed; several minutes of this refreshing process would pass and then the device would go dead and not allow me to restart it. I held down the button for several seconds as instructed. Still, the device would not let me restart it. I charged it using its cord and my computer, but the device told me there was no battery power. I tried transferring music in MP3 format directly to its memory from my computer; the music wouldn't transfer over. I could go on and on. Just save your money and pay more for something better than this waste of time, space, and energy.

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White This was purchased as a gift. I, the writer of this review, am the recipient of the gift. After about a year of "monkeying around" with this piece of technology, I have unplugged it and relegated it to a drawer. It simply doesn't work consistently. It often " has trouble connecting to the internet", even though nothing has changed. It often gets the voice commands wrong, or just doesn't respond. When it is working, (we use it mostly to stream music to a sound bar that I bought just to use with the dot by Blue tooth connection), it will often just quit, or pause and restart. I have had several conversations with the help desk at Amazon, and although very pleasant, the solution always seems to be the same. Turn it off and reinstall it. Not doing that any more. The WiFi is one room away, and lap tops, tablets and smart phones all work just fine in this room and others through out the house. It is sad, because this seemed like a great solution to get some music into this room without blasting it from several rooms away, but alas, it is a bust. Some of the things that it did, like the "this day in history" were fun, or the jokes she would tell were so silly that they were just funny, but that doesn't make the Dot worth the time, effort, or money. Save your money and buy a Blue tooth speaker for your phone. You'll be glad you did.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
Aftershokz Xtrainerz Bone Conduction MP3 Swimming Headphones with Swim Cap, Black Diamond Pros:
It is hard to find a really good swimming headset. This is it. (I have tried many other types, and this is the winner for me.)
SO easy to charge. So easy to load music. Allows for folders (my other headphones don't).
Weighs NOTHING. You don't know you have it on! Doesn't press to hard or hurt anywhere. A lot of bone conduction headsets are uncomfortable but this one is not.
Has a huge battery life. Also it TELLS you every time you turn it on how much battery is left. (If you want to check after you are done, turn it off and on again and it will tell you.)
Controls make sense. Mostly. A few features require long push and hold to activate, but the stuff you use daily is intuitive.
Volume is good. Not super loud, but also you can adjust the placement around your ear to be louder/softer.

Cons:
The band is longer than I need. So there is a gap at the back of my head. I wish it were a little smaller.
The buttons are a little fidgety. They are so small and all feel alike so it takes a while to feel your way around and figure out which button is which. I wish they would put the power and mode buttons on one side and the Plus/minus buttons on the other ear. Or put the plus minus on the outside rather than under edge.
That said, I put my 400 songs on it and just let it play while I workout.
This one is petty but there are 2 modes - water and regular. It changes the EQ to supposedly sound better underwater vs. on land. But I find the on land mode sounds better in water. BUT I don't use earplugs. So maybe that is why.
text_fidelity_b: Aftershokz Xtrainerz Bone Conduction MP3 Swimming Headphones with Swim Cap, Black Diamond

HAYLOU True Wireless Earbuds, GT1 Bluetooth 5.0 Sports HD Stereo Touch Control Ear Buds with IPX5 Waterproof/Fast Connection/Mini Case(Only 30g)/Total 12H Playtime (Dark Grey) I’ve tested a few similar sets of ear buds with mixed results but I was really impressed with this set.

I read the instruction manual - removed the tiny stickers on each ear bud and plugged in the case. It achieved a full charge in just over an hour.

I removed the ear buds from the case, the right one first and then the left and they paired with each other immediately. I went to my Bluetooth settings in my iPhone and found Haylou-GT1_R and my phone paired with the set with no issue.

I was surprised at the sound quality these tiny ear buds deliver. They can definitely be turned up as loud as you’d want to listen. The bass, midtones and treble is on par for ear buds - even those that are much larger.

I did figure out that the initial way I had them in my ears was upside down when I went to test the calling features. The microphone needs to be pointed towards your mouth for best audio reception and sound quality improves a bit in this position.

Call quality was excellent for both hearing the other person and them hearing you.

In my testing the earbuds had no problem receiving within the 33’ stated range (actually making it to around 40’) and even received clearly through multiple walls - 2 rooms away with the doors closed and many obstacles in between.

The only issue I struggled with was tapping the ear bud to stop / start the music and answer / end calls / activate voice assistant and skip tracks. There is no button, you just tap an area of the exterior of the ear bud but you have to tap a very exact area which isn’t necessary easy to locate as it is not differentiated from the rest. It would have been helpful if the manufacturer put a different texture in that area so you could feel it with your finger to locate it.

While the manufacturers claims these last for 12 hours I found it was closer to 8 under normal use - still excellent. And the case will charge them without it having to be plugged back in which is always a nice feature.

These earbuds excelled in all of my tests showing that they are a high quality, dependable product.

This is a set I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend.

⭐️As with all Drew’s Reviews, if I discover something new about this product - good or bad - I will UPDATE my review. I believe in creating detailed, complete reviews because, like you, I depend on them when I am shopping. If you found my review HELPFUL - please click ⬇️ below!⭐️

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage Bought this router a few days ago and have already begun the return process. I didn't have a good gut feeling about this router from the start, partly because the reviews are not all raves and partly simply because it looks kind of...evil to me. I am definitely not a fan of the hyper-aggressive router design trend that seems to be targeted at adolescent male gamers. I do not look at this thing and think it looks cool and feel positive feelings; I look at it and feel...apprehension. As a physical object, it's not something I really want in my apartment. But I decided to give it a try anyway because I don't think that kind of gut feeling should be one's primary consideration in choosing a router, and because I often like having the latest, cutting-edge tech and thought it would be nice to be ready for Wifi 6 for when I eventually get an iPhone 11 or some other device that features that protocol. But unfortunately, the negative experiences do not come only when I look at the thing.

I was at first alarmed, as I set up the router, by what a very long time it took anything to happen in the app. At every point at which I so much as switched to a different screen in the app, both during and after setup, the app would chug for an alarmingly long time before finally displaying the page I'd navigated to. This is to be expected when the router needs to restart, but...these were not points at which the router needed to restart. These were not points at which I'd changed any setting at all. These were points at which nothing at all had happened except that I'd attempted to go from, say, the app's main page to the Device Manager page, or the Wifi Settings page, or wherever. Simply switching pages in the app would take 20 or 30 seconds or longer. Another negative first impression.

I also noticed that the app doesn't give me access to a lot of the features of the router I expect to have access to. Granted, I'm an advanced user compared to a lot of people - networking is an aspect of computing I've enjoyed mucking around in for decades now, and my inclination with a new router (or an old one, for that matter) is to dive straight into areas of the settings where many ordinary users may fear to tread. But the Nighthawk phone app appears to be targeted more toward the average consumer. Which, if you're more the average consumer, is fine. But if you're me, you find that to be a disappointing restriction.

Then I started trying to use the web UI instead, and while it gave me access to all those more techy parameters I sought, I found the same delay problem happening when I tried to switch from one page of settings to another, but here it happened for longer, and sometimes the target page wouldn't load at all until I clicked again, this time on the blank page with the spinning progress indicator in the center.

So both of the means I have for interfacing with the router are inordinately slow, and one of them is clunky and glitchy on top of it.

And finally, add to all this the way I will occasionally go to navigate to any ordinary webpage and be told my browser can't display the page because I'M NOT CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET, and voila! - the straw that broke the proverbial camel's back.

This happens, and I go and look at the router to see if maybe it's restarted itself for some reason (automatic software update?) and...no. All lights are on and looking as they do during normal operation; the router's just not providing said normal operation.

I never once had such problems with the Apple AirPort Extreme I replaced with this router, nor with the Linksys AC5400 I bought more recently and then wound up giving to a friend. So, because I want a router that, unlike the AirPort Extreme, is tri-band, is still supported with software/firmware updates, and might also feature better performance with multiple connected devices, I bought myself another AC5400 with which I will be replacing this unsatisfactory Netgear thing as soon as it arrives.

And also because I decided I can wait for Wifi 6 until such time as I actually do have devices capable of taking advantage of it, which may be quite some time (i just bought a new MacBook Pro which doesn't support it, and I don't see the iPhone 11 as having any compelling advantages over my iPhone XS Max, soooo...).

The Linksys AC5400 is a monster among 802.11ac routers and has garnered much respect in tech mags and blogs and so forth. Plus I myself have about a year's experience with one and it's been fast, reliable, and glitch-free. So if you're looking for a new router and don't feel compelled to buy into 802.11ax just yet (few devices support it yet anyways), I heartily recommend that one.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage

14AWG conductors and ground mean you can get the maximum out of most household circuits (because most are 15 amp). I don't like any extension cords or strips less than that to avoid voltage drop, overloading, etc.

text_fidelity_a:
CyberPower CSP604UMP6 Professional Surge Protector, 1200J/125V, 6 Outlets, 2 USB Charge Ports, 4ft Power Cord, 6 Pack , Black The irony here is that I bought this to replace a 20 year old surge protector whose opposite end from where the power cable enters the device was getting so hot, the beige plastic was showing burn marks. I thought with all the technological advancements, 6 AC plugs (the same as the old one) and 2 USB ports, I should fit a device or 2 extra on the new one. Nope. These plugs are so close together, even a plug that is just slightly larger than a standard grounded plug will cause an overlap on the plug next to it thereby rendering the neighboring plug unavailable. Despite going from an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip to an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip, I went from being able to fit 5 plugs in the old strip to only being able, in the best configuration possible, to fit 4 plugs.

I was lucky that I had one plug that was a Samsung wall charger with a Samsung USB charger cable. Since I had to lose something, that was the only one I could lose, but still put on the strip. So what? I was not expecting to lose 1 of the 2 USB chargers to accommodate one of the plugs that had to get bumped.

I probably would have gotten over that, but then when I went to test the performance of the USB charging ports, they fell short. With the Samsung manufactured original cable for my S5, this port only charged at 1.15A. To validate it, I took it to several other devices in the house and with the same S5 device, Samsung wall plug and original cable and the same meter, the S5 pulled 1.75A out of both the Samsung wall charger and the 5 port USB charger that I also bought from Amazon (I have a review there, too).

I gave it 2 stars because overall, this is not such a disaster that I would waste my time and money returning it. There are soooo many surge protector power chargers with USB charge ports on Amazon that at least one of them has to be better than this.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CSP604UMP6 Professional Surge Protector, 1200J/125V, 6 Outlets, 2 USB Charge Ports, 4ft Power Cord, 6 Pack , Black

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen Frustrating. Could not get the iPhone app to work at all, I'd slide the WiFi button to be informed that the WiFi was not functioning. Do I need to set up a local hotspot to use the WiFi feature to download the videos? Which appears to be about the only distinguishing feature of this dashcam. This is NOT a Sony product, apparently it uses licensed Sony technology. The dashcam itself is reasonably well designed. There's a horrid mechanical-female voice which I don't see how to disable. The user experience overall is poor. The manual is not bad as far as legibility, but the content is minimum. Minimal content in four or five languages.

The mounting scheme is atrocious, a joke. I'm not going to put self-adhesive cable anchors anywhere in my car, period. It's just plain dumb. I'm tempted to use a suction cup mount from another dashcam. Or cable ties on my rear-view mirror. But if you're homebrewing a solution right out of the box, maybe you're better off with another product altogether. The mounting suggestion is just a show-stopper. Not a good thing.

The video itself seems good, I mean, dashcams in general are fascinating and useful. But if you're expecting to have consumers put something in their car, it had been not involve defacing any part of the car or reducing its value. Leftover adhesive footprints would be an obvious problem.

I'm uploading a photo of the box. Green type on a black background. Not really a great design. Generally type and packaging tells you more about a product than the manufacturer might have intended. Just not that sophisticated.

Overall there are better dashcams out there. The ability to use WiFi to download video from the camera seemed promising, but I couldn't get it to work at all. The audio feedback from the device was far too loud and I couldn't turn it off. The mounting idea was dead on arrival, not happening.

Disappointing. Cannot recommend this product. A swing and a miss, as they say in baseball.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen

text_fidelity_a:
ClearStream Micron-R Indoor HDTV Antenna with Reflector - 35 Mile Range I have a roof-top antenna that worked well for analog stations but, when I converted to digital, I went from receiving 8 stations to just 1. After trying a few other antennas, I came across the ClearStream 4. I'm able to pull in 20+ digital stations perfectly, and 4 more so-so. Several analog stations come in as well, but the picture is not nearly as good as the digitial stations.

The antenna is well-made, but is a bit of a pain to assemble - lots of pieces to screw together. It only takes about 10 minutes, but you'll probably need to utter a few choice words since it's hard to get the screws to line up properly. The directions are pretty spotty, but give you the essential information. The brackets are heavy-duty, and everything is either aluminum or plastic, so it should hold up well to the elements if I put it outside. Right now, it is in my attic, and may stay there since it pulls in all the stations I want to watch. It does not come with a cable.

It's pretty compact given its performance, and much more compact that the DB8 (another Antenna Direct model with about the same specifications). Very happy with the performance. Also have a DB2 -- see my comments on that review that compare it to this antenna in terms of performance.
text_fidelity_b: ClearStream Micron-R Indoor HDTV Antenna with Reflector - 35 Mile Range

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

text_fidelity_a:
2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters Likes.

Well made.
Long cord. The long cord is very important.

Setup.

I used the long cord to place it on the floor, next to my patio door.
I then set my TV to auto scan.
It gave me many more stations than my non amplified leaf antennae pulled in.
Every station was crystal clear.
However, that was not a convenient permanent location, so I then placed it behind the TV.
It was important to first place it in the best possible area, in my case against the patio door to identify all possible stations.

Issues.

After auto scan identified all possible stations, I moved the antenna to behind my entertainment center. I lost half the stations. But, the TV showed those station numbers, it just couldn't pull them in. I then placed it flat on top of the entertainment center. It improved the reception. I then slid it partially inside my TV wall mount hardware, flat against the wall. It gave me excellent reception on all identified stations.

My advice.

Take advantage of the long cord, move it next to a window even if it won't be left there. You can then place the antenna in more convenient locations, trying to get back to as many identified stations as possible.
text_fidelity_b: 2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver) I've only had the Fujifilm X-E2 camera and 18-55mm lens for a short while and I've barely scratched the surface of it's capabilities. This is a camera anyone can use right out of the box but also one that you can spend years learning to master.

The retro look and styling are very attractive but they made it, for me at least who was used to an extended grip on the camera body, a little hard to handle. I found myself hitting the AE-L and AF-L buttons often and frequently by accident spun the exposure compensation dial without even realizing I had. I resolved this with the LensMate Thumb Grip designed for the X-E1/E2. It made a good camera great. I also added LensMate's brass soft release button to the shutter release. It does aid in smoother pressing of the shutter button but it also looks great on the camera.

The 18-55mm lens that comes with the X-E2 is a real pleasure to use. The zoom is stiff enough to let you feel in control but easy enough that you don't need brute force to use it.

Image quality, even at 100%, is outstanding. I've been getting so many 'keepers' that I've had to reevaluate my shooting style. I feel like I'm overshooting. In the past I was shooting three or four hundred images in an outing and getting maybe four or six shots I really want to keep and share. Now, with the X-E2 I'm finding two, three even four times that many shots that are worth keeping. I'm going to need a bigger hard drive!

Battery life has been pretty good for me. Even shooting in temperatures down in the 30's and 40's I had no problem taking well over three hundred images and still having battery bars left. In the times I've gone out all day wandering around the county I've yet to have to swap out the battery though I did purchase an extra just to have around.

Functionality, configurability and controls are extensive and a bit quirky but easy enough to get used to. As an example the Q button gives you 'Q'uick access to many of the more necessary and often used controls. You navigate around the Q menu with the 5-way controller but you make setting changes with the command dial. One of the features I found most interesting was the ability to constrain the ISO in Auto mode and set a minimum shutter speed. I also liked the ability to configure the four letter prefix for file names. All the 'extra' settings like special effects, double exposure, movie mode and panorama are accessed through the Drive button.

I did find a couple small negatives. Nothing to cause me not to want to use it but made me wonder. The odd menu systems. The pop-up flash is a bit anemic and is somewhat blocked by the 18-55mm lens. It's even worse when the hood is attached. The shoulder strap that comes with the camera... I know they're usually bad but this is cheap camera bad not quality camera bad. I put it around my neck, gave a tug, and then threw it away without putting it on the camera. I expected a little more quality there. The tulip lens hood that comes with the 18-55mm feels hard and brittle. It too could have been a bit better quality. I already mentioned the LensMate thumb grip that I think is an absolute must add item (it's really worth the cost). My big clumsy hands desperately needed it to aid in stability and control.

Where to start with a conclusion? This is an interesting mix of old school retro styling and modern camera technology. I think Fuji have really blended them together well. I can see myself enjoying this camera for years to come. Very highly recommended.

{Update}
Not wanting to pile on the negatives but I had intended to and completely forgot to mention the battery door. It's really kind of flimsy and feels like it could easily break. Also, with the way it's hinged I find it rather hard to get the memory card out of the camera because it's so close and parallel to the battery door's hinge.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver)

Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue I was so excited to receive these headphones and give them a go. I’ve spent right at a week with them and this is what I’ve found.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. Once I had everything set up, it was easy. I would have rather had a semblance of instruction than the wild packaging. The headphones were easy to pair to my phone and the sound is crystal clear. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue
