text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics USB 3.1 Type-C to 4-Port Aluminum Hub Connector, Black One of the problems I have seen with the latest crop of notebooks and Ultrabooks that have come out is a lack of USB ports. There's usually a need for more ports than these systems have and it gets frustrating. A small USB hub like this is a good solution. That said, this particular hub does not have a separate power source so some consideration must be made when plugging in power-hungry devices.

From a design stantpoint this is a solid unit, shaped to be accessible without being huge. It has a little weight to it and this is helpful for keeping it stable. The addition of Velcro strips in the package to secure it in one place is a welcome inclusion and makes securing the hub very simple no matter what your configuration is.

The hub provides four USB 3.1 type A ports. Let me state what should be obvious - this will not convert a USB 1.1 or 2.0 port into a 3.1 port, so plug it into a 3.1 port if you want the speed across the hub. For my specific uses, it does not need to be a high-speed hub and I am find with using it as a 2.0 hub, but admittedly that's slightly wasteful.

There is no power port on this hub and there is no DC adapter in the box. So, any power that the hub needs comes through the onboard port into which it is plugged. That's fine for low-power devices like mice, keyboards, memory sticks and so on, but if the intent is to plug in such things as USB hard drives with no external power supply this can cause some headaches. No, one drive isn't going to overload the hub, but if you have multiple drives attached there may be reliability issues when they starve one another for power. When the device plugged in has its own power supply (like a big backup drive), this has little impact on the hub.

The point is, plan carefully how you intend to use the hub.

I like this hub and it does a good job for what it is. It has given me three extra ports on an Ultrabook I use which is all I could ask for. The ability to power this hub with it's own power supply would be the only area for improvement I could find.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics USB 3.1 Type-C to 4-Port Aluminum Hub Connector, Black

Logitech MK235 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo for Windows, USB Receiver, 15 FN Keys, Long Battery Life, Compatible with PC, Laptop I have to say right up front that I am NOT a tech expert by any means. I just simply know when something works well and when it doesn't.

I've purchased three of these keyboard/mouse sets since January 2018 and I think it's one of the best pieces of equipment that I've added to my computer set up. I run 3 to 4 laptops every day, each one accomplishes a different task for me. It was getting to be a real pain having to stand up and stretch across the desk to enter a password or move the mouse and these solved that problem for me. It did take some getting used to at first since each set looks exactly alike but I have that worked out with their placements. LOL!

The set in the photo is the first set that I purchased on January 29, 2018. This set is used for HOURS darn near every day. I write online content so my keyboards always take a beating. This one has held up BEAUTIFULLY and, as a bonus, I've only had to replace the battery in the mouse once. My guess is that somehow I got super charged batteries in the keyboard because it is still going on the originals. The other two sets are still running off of 100% original batteries.

There isn't one thing that I can complain about with this set. I like that there are little flip out legs on the bottom/back part of the keyboard that allow it to lean up in the back. It makes it much easier to use. I like that there can be some distance between the keyboard/mouse and the computer when being used and I LOVE that there are no wires to deal with.

All in all it's a great set that is worth the money. I have three of these sets and each one is fantastic.

Because of this, I found out my mac uses about 50Watts in idle, and about 105 when doing heavy video processing. It's a great way to monitor power usage. Plenty of power ports in the back and seem easily capable of powering the mac for about 30 minutes. It even has a test mode that switches it to battery power without unplugging anything

Samsung Galaxy Watch 3 (45mm, GPS, Bluetooth) Smart Watch with Advanced Health Monitoring, Fitness Tracking, and Long Lasting Battery - Mystic Black (US Version) (Renewed) I got Moto 360 several years ago when smart watches first came out and it was nice, but annoying. It was tied into everything and kept giving me alerts and so eventually I got tired of it. My wife also had a first generation Samsung Gear watch and that was about the same as the Moto.
Well, fast forward a few years and now my wife, daughter, son and daughter-in-law all have newer smart watches (Apple Watches and Fitbit) and they all love them. It was time to get a new phone, so I got a Samsung S20 FE and then decided to get the Samsung watch. I saw on the reviews that it really works well with Samsung phones and so I decided to get the Watch 3. I was looking at the Watch 2, which had a few less features and then I found the Watch 3 in the 41mm size and then found a refurbished one so I ended up paying about the same for the Watch 3 as I would have for the Watch 2.
I'm very impressed with the watch and really love it. I didn't get the one with a cell phone, it just connects to my phone with bluetooth and/or wifi, but it's really amazing. I get my messages, and can turn off the ones that I don't want and then I also get all the health apps. So, now it tells me to get off my chair and walk around and does EKG and stress tesing and Oxygen levels..
I was concerned that the 41 mm might be too small, but it is a great size for me as you can see from the pic. I have had a Citizen Echo Drive for more than 10 years and it is a little larger, but I like the size of the Watch 3 better.
If you are thinking about getting a watch, this one is a good deal right now and I believe it does work best if you use it with a Samsung phone.

The screen is sharp and readable in 2240 x 1400 pixels mode. This model does NOT have a touch screen, so if that's important to you, you need to look at other laptops that sport that feature. The system so far is quick to respond to requests and has sufficient RAM and storage space.

One nice feature missing from all the other laptops I’ve owned or used is an automatic power up whenever the computer case is opened. There is also a power button in case you need it.

Beside Windows 11 Pro, this machine comes with significant value added: a year subscription to Microsoft Office 365 (normally $69.99/year) and also a two-year subscription to McAfee LiveSafe security suite (normally $129.99/year).

Most people who use laptops probably don’t mind that this machine, like most laptops now, does not have an ethernet port. However, WiFi seems to be performing well in its absence. I may not be the typical user, but I prefer the option to connect by ethernet.

I work almost exclusively at a desk with the power supply connected, so I have not tested the battery life of this Dell. My only real complaint is that, owing to the 14” display size, the keyboard is correspondingly smaller than I like. If I were to do much typing, I’d probably plug in an external keyboard. If your hands are smaller than mine are, this won't be much of an issue for you.

As has been mentioned in other reviews, this is not a gamer’s dream machine. It’s for normal office and business use. Its compact size makes it good for the road.

text_fidelity_a: Echo Flex - Plug-in mini smart speaker with Alexa I have Echo devices of one kind or another in every room and have had others that I’ve decided to let go (original Echo and Echo Auto). They’ve all performed their smarthome duties acceptably well. My biggest complaint across the board is sound quality. Alexa always sounds like she’s talking to you from underneath a pile of pillows. Bass? Sure, on the Echo Show, at least. Treble? Nada. Sure, you can use the app’s “equalizer”... but it’d take an oscilloscope to detect the minuscule difference that makes in the sound quality. I’d given up on getting any more devices... until I saw a review of the Flex on Paul Hibbert’s YouTube channel... he liked it, but said (I think) that it sounded ‘trebly’. Trebly?! That’s a magic word to my ears. I ordered one up and found that it indeed sounds ‘trebly’ (call it tinny of you like) but who cares? Who seriously listens to music on these tiny little devices anyway?! I can understand what Alexa says now - all the plosives are there. I still wonder why Amazon can’t tune the rest of the Alexa enabled devices for better higher frequency clarity.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Flex - Plug-in mini smart speaker with Alexa

Taking it out of the box, I was able to tell that it is well-built and well thought out. The solar panel is of good quality and can be mounted on the camera or separately. The necessary USB extension cable and extra mounting arm is included in this camera kit if you decide to mount the panel separately from the camera. Mounting is easy. Just two screws into the eaves and you're done. No wires to pull and no batteries to change. Compare this with systems like Arlo where you would need to break out your ladder to switch out batteries every month or spend extra to purchase a solar panel for each camera.

This camera has all of the standard functions of live feed, motion detection, and night vision but of course it also has the pan and tilt function which helps to get a clearer picture of what you're trying to see. Local SD card storage means that a subscription service isn't necessary to review past events. It's all quite nice. I did find that there is a significant lag in the camera. It can take a full second for any pan and tilt commands to actually go through.

This camera works with the Tuya app (also works with Smart Life) so it's up to you to decide how much you can trust those apps, but otherwise the camera is a solid purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch The positives about these headphones outnumber the negatives.

In no particular order;

1. Easy set up. Like all bluetooth devices, these headphones were a quick set up by simply turning them on and my mac responded with 'Do You Want To Use This Device?' The total set up time, approximately sixty seconds!

2.Excellent for VOIP gmail phone.

3. You can charge the headset, while you are using it. So on marathon conference call days, I can plug them in, while using them for about twenty minutes and then they are charged enough to last through a long, boring, three hour conference call (more's the pity!).

4. They charge off the USB port and they come with a cable for doing this.

5. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, so no headaches!

6. Adjustable volume which is perfect for the hard of hearing.

The negatives, in no particular order;

1. The sound quality is not so great. It is too grainy for music, there is a static sound in the background of everything you are listening to, not a big deal if you are using them for phone conversations, but a definite loser if you are trying to listen to music.

2. It gets more static background noise as the batteries wind down.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch

text_fidelity_a:
Rolling Spider I'm kind of them on this. It has its flaws no doubt, but it is a lot of fun.

The app you need is Free Flight 3. It doesn't say that anywhere in the instructions. There are training videos on YouTube that are helpful in figuring out how to use this. Definitely worth watching. The app itself is unintuitive and hard to use. Once you get used tip it, though it's pretty cool.

The drone can handle crashing into just about anything, and I know this because we were so bad at this we crashed it into just about everything except the cat. The cat didn't want to be in the same room with it. The blades can't break skin if you crash it into yourself. We had that happen too. The axle gets very hot from the friction though.

I like that is so tiny it can launch off your hand and fly or roll it indoors. I don't like the battery life. You get about five minutes of play time per charge. I like the appearance of the drone. It's very cute and comes with stickers.

Overall it's entertaining, but the battery life needs to improve before it's worth more than three stars.

The battery
text_fidelity_b: Rolling Spider

text_fidelity_a:
Connectland CL-U2MNHUB-4B 4 Ports USB V2.0 Mini Hub (Black) I bought this hub in tandem with a cooling pad to use my laptop as a desktop replacement; I was running out of USB ports (my laptop only has 3) and this would double that number for less than $10. I wasn't sure if, since this hub isn't powered, I would be able to connect my speakers and cooling pad (both of which are powered over USB) with this hub, but I decided to take a chance and they both work perfectly when connected through the hub. It has exceeded all my expectations. Even better, each port has an on/off switch with LED indicator lights so if you're not using something, you can turn it off without unplugging it from the hub.

Pros
-able to run powered things like a cooling pad (for me, at least; your mileage may vary)
-small so it can be easily tucked out of sight
-on/off switches for each port

Cons
-LED indicator lights (I don't find them distracting because they are so small and don't blink, but some people might)
-removing USB connectors can be a little difficult, but that just means they won't fall out while you're trying to use something
(these are both a little nit-picky, I know, but I really have nothing bad to say about this product)

I've only owned it for a week, so I will update my review if anything changes.
text_fidelity_b: Connectland CL-U2MNHUB-4B 4 Ports USB V2.0 Mini Hub (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam [[VIDEOID:bcc01f35bd32d1e66d3df81c3dace063]] Updated as promised: After working with the company I was able to completely secure the camera and still access it remotely. After all the initial problems and concerns I have had it installed and working for about a month I guess. It's working great on a variety of different software and protocols. I even tried connecting it to the Angelcam website and using DDNS. Works great with just about everything. With the 128GB SD card it does great. I uploaded some new photos of it working and the different clients being used securely. This turned out to be a great buy because the image quality is incredible and it's got an incredibly wide angle.

You cannot see the IR light like that at night it's only because of the camera I used you can see it. I did that for a reason so that everyone could see the amount of IR light it puts out. The infrared works great as you can see but the motion sensor even on the least sensitive setting picks up rains and bugs flying in front of it. Almost all motion sensors do. The audio sensor works great but the alarm feature doesn't because it's only one way audio. The email was easy to setup once you know which smtp server your ISP uses which WOW doesn't like giving theirs out even to paying customers. The video was provided by them and helped a lot because the screws were impossible to see and there are unnecessary ones in there that don't need to be removed. I have posted the material they sent me as well. I hope this helps everyone out.

BEFORE EDIT AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT:
So far I have had a lot of issues with this camera and still haven't got it to where I would trust letting it outside my isolated LAN which mean I cannot view remotely as of yet. I changed the 32Gb SD card out to a 128Gb card after contacting support since there is no instructions online or anywhere else on how to do it. Turns out it's the one tiny screw in on the top to remove the black piece and then you must carefully unscrew the lens cap. After that you will find several screws lowered besides the lens and IR area. You only need to remove the 4 of the screws. If you look really close with magnification you can see exactly what screws you need to remove because you can see how they hold the board underneath in place. Underneath the lens is the board that holds the SD-Card. Their support was nice enough to send me a video later on. I plan on posting that later after I get this all working. As of now it is telling me I need to reset the camera and there is no reset button that I can find. I am guessing it must be on that board again which means I am going to have to pull the whole thing apart again. In my opinion this is very poorly designed and not very good for people who like to customize or configure their devices. I do not like the way the it acts as soon as it connects to your network. I am still working on testing and hope I can get these issues resolved soon. The picture quality is great but there is a serious lack of security and other major issues plaguing this device. I am going to do some further testing and contact support once again about resetting this camera hopefully without having to dissemble it again but I don't see how. It has been disconnected for hours without power and will not reset that way. I also notice that the camera unit get's extremely hot for some reason. This will defiantly shorten it's life span. More to come on this product but for now I do not recommend buying this unless you are familiar with IP camera installation, network configuration, and have some electrical experience as far as handling circuit boards. This has been a real pain in the read since day one but I am hoping it will be worth it but time will tell. I will upload the video provided by them after getting their consent.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam
